correctness.rationale: In n=2, the wedge metric projection is a continuous piecewise linear selection of identity, zero and rank-one ray projections with coefficients (κ^{q-1}t±u)/(1+κ^q). Exact ℓp→ℓp rank-one operator norm equals [(1+κ^p)^{1/p}(1+κ^{q(q-1)})^{1/q}]/(1+κ^q); finite linear-region segmentation gives global norm and an interior ray region gives sharpness. Hölder equality occurs exactly at p=2 or κ=1. For n≥3 independently checked boundary y=(κ,c,s), outward normal f=(-1,κc,κs), v=J_q(f), tangency h=(κc,1,0), and nonzero dual derivative ⟨J_p(h),v⟩=(κc)^{q-1}-(κc)^{p-1} whenever p≠2 and κc≠1. First-order convex KKT ensures P(y+δv)=y; a nearby cone-boundary z(η) gives strict expansion. For p=2 Hilbert projection is 1-Lipschitz; n=1 is positive-part. Calculated planar sample constants at (p,κ)=(1.5,.3),(3,1),(4,2) match the stated formula; finite tests are not proof. Proof addresses all positive slopes but makes no quantitative claim for n≥3 beyond nonexpansivity failure.
